subject: Availability pledge exception request — CumulusAI onboarding trial
messages:
From: Jorge Silva <jorge@cumulusai.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Availability pledge for onboarding trial

Vanessa —

Thanks again for the call last week. As CumulusAI ramps our pilot, we want to request a short-term availability pledge for the onboarding period. Specifically: a three-month pilot window where we get a 99.95% availability pledge for our production inference endpoints used by our early customers. The reasons are:

- We’re running parallel rollouts with partners and any sustained downtime would stop signups.
- We’ll send heavy traffic spikes as we stress test the system during integration.

We understand this is outside standard terms. Can you outline the internal approval path, expected guardrails, and any temporary mitigations you’d require (rate limits, feature gates, ops playbook)? I’ve attached a short SOW outlining the onboarding milestones. We’re prepared to sign a targeted MOP and commit to a runbook exercise.

Attachment: cumulus_onboarding_sow.pdf (PDF)

Jorge Silva
Director of Platform
CumulusAI
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.com, connor_obrien@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Cc: Jorge Silva <jorge@cumulusai.com>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 12:04:00 -07:00
Subject: FW: Availability pledge for onboarding trial

Folks — forwarding CumulusAI's ask. High-level: they want a 99.95% availability pledge for a 3-month onboarding/trial. They’ve attached the SOW.

Proposed internal ask:
- Product: confirm whether we can carve out a short-term SLA guardrail for a subset of endpoints and the expected product constraints.
- SRE: outline required operational mitigations (runbook, autoscale headroom, fallback model) we need before committing.
- Legal: draft short, time-boxed exception language and a simple MOP signature page.

My suggested constraints to start the conversation (feel free to edit):
- Timeboxed pilot: 90 days maximum.
- Scope-limited: apply pledge only to listed production endpoints in SOW.
- Conditional fallback: automatic model downgrade or throttling if capacity thresholds exceeded.
- Error budget & reporting: daily availability reports + weekly exec summary.

Attachments: cumulus_onboarding_sow.pdf (from customer)

Can we turn around guidance within 48 business hours? Jorge is pushing a partner demo 9/6. I’ll own communicating back.

— Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: FW: Availability pledge for onboarding trial

Thanks — low-lift operational stance first: I can support a time-limited availability pledge provided we bake in the following required mitigations and acceptance criteria:

1) Ops runbook signed-off and exercised before pilot start (playbook to include failover steps, traffic shaping ramp plan, alert thresholds).
2) Dedicated pool reservation or guaranteed headroom on dedicated hosts for the pilot (minimum X vGPU instances — I put a placeholder in the attached draft).
3) Automatic fallback to a pinned, lower-throughput model variant when KV cache or serving latency crosses threshold.
4) Error-budget clause: if we hit >2 incidents consuming >80% of error budget in 30 days, the pledge pauses and we execute the escalation runbook.

I drafted a minimal ops_runbook-draft.md and a quick checklist — attaching. I’ll need product to guarantee what endpoints are in/out and whether model pinning is feasible in the short window.

Attachment: ops_runbook-draft.md

— Connor O'Brien
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, connor_obrien@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 11:37:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: FW: Availability pledge for onboarding trial

Appreciate the quick turnaround. A few product constraints and alternatives:

- Full-platform 99.95% is risky for a short, unproven workload unless we reserve capacity. We should avoid a blanket SLA change.
- Alternative A: timeboxed 99.95% for an explicit list of endpoints (as Vanessa suggested) + feature gating so we can toggle traffic to those endpoints.
- Alternative B: standard platform SLA (99.8) + a higher-priority burst capacity guarantee for the pilot window (this buys headroom without changing SLA language broadly).

I need finance to estimate cost impact for reserved capacity — Vanessa, can you ask for an expected peak QPS and percent of traffic that needs the pledge? Connor, your runbook draft looks good; we’ll need to confirm model pinning feasibility with inference infra (I can loop in infra if required).

Next step: if we agree on a short list of endpoints and an explicit traffic cap, I can draft the product acceptance criteria (behavioral and telemetry checks) we’ll need in the MOP.

— Aditya Rao
Head of Product, Core Serving
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Jorge Silva <jorge@cumulusai.com>, legal@cumulusai.com
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com, connor_obrien@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2026 14:03:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Availability pledge for onboarding trial — proposed path

Jorge — thanks for the patience. Internal alignment notes below and a proposed short path to get you live by 9/10 while limiting risk for both sides.

Summary of what we can commit to today (subject to signatures & checklist):
- Timeboxed pledge: 99.95% availability applied to a short list of production endpoints for 90 days from pilot start.
- Scope & controls: pledge applies only to endpoints listed in the attached SOW. We will apply traffic caps and feature gates; automatic model downgrade will activate on sustained latency/regression.
- Operational readiness: we require sign-off on the runbook and a pre-launch run of the failover playbook.
- Reporting: daily availability dashboard and weekly executive summary; CumulusAI to receive incident postmortems for any outage.

Open items for signoff (what we need from you):
1) Confirm expected peak QPS and percent of total traffic for endpoints in scope (this impacts reserved capacity).
2) Sign the short MOP page (I can send a 1-page MOP for signature).
3) Agree to the error-budget pause clause (if invoked, pledge pauses and partner demo may be delayed).

Next internal steps: Aditya will produce acceptance criteria, Connor will finalize runbook, Neha will draft the MOP/exception language. Vanessa will own customer communication and timelines.

Attachments: cumulus_onboarding_sow.pdf, ops_runbook-draft.md, capacity_cost_estimate.xlsx

If that works I’ll send the 1-page MOP and a short form signature page for Cumulus lawyers. We aim to have internal approvals by EOD Friday so we can meet your demo timeline.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this moving.

— Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
